subject: Clarification: which request/response items are retained by default?
body:
---- Message 1 (2028-05-11T09:12:00-07:00) ----
From: Lina Park <lina.park@acme.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example.com
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on what Redwood stores by default (prompts/outputs)

Hi Vivek,

Hope you’re well. As part of our procurement/security review I need a precise, plain-language answer for what Redwood stores by default when we send inference requests to the hosted API. Specifically:
- Do you store the raw prompt text we send?
- Are generated outputs (responses) persisted and for how long?
- Do you persist intermediate/partial streaming tokens or only final responses?
- Do you retain embeddings, model logs, or KV cache artifacts by default?

We need this for our internal data classification and to map to our retention rules. Please keep it short and call out any differences for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Thanks,
Lina Park
Procurement, Acme Analytics

---- Message 2 (2028-05-11T11:03:00-07:00) ----
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example.com>
To: Lina Park <lina.park@acme.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on what Redwood stores by default (prompts/outputs)

Hi Lina — quick answers below, then a short rationale and deletion paths. Happy to hop on a quick call if you want a blow-by-blow.

Short answers (hosted Redwood API, default behavior):
- Raw prompts (request text and associated metadata): retained by Redwood for 45 days by default. This is used for billing, fraud detection, and quality monitoring.
- Generated outputs (final response text): retained for 90 days by default to support debugging, replay, and our quality/regression tooling.
- Streaming/partial tokens: not persisted as separate artifacts. The system assembles the final response; only the final response is written to logs.
- Embeddings: not retained by default beyond 7 days. We keep them briefly for cache hits and duplicate detection; customers can opt out or request deletion sooner.
- KV cache / runtime ephemeral state: never persisted to the customer-facing log store — ephemeral only in the execution plane and cleared per-request.

Dedicated and Private:
- Dedicated: retention defaults are configurable by customer; our managed Dedicated offering ships with a 30-day default but customers can set retention in the Console or via the API and can request Redwood-managed purges.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): Redwood does not retain inference logs in our control plane unless the customer opts in. Retention is customer-controlled and governed by their own infrastructure and KMS.

Deletion and opt-out:
- Customers can opt out of storing request/response logs for new traffic via the Console toggle or the data_controls API; opt-outs apply prospectively (not retroactive) unless a data-erase request is submitted.
- For retroactive deletions we support a Data Erasure API and run a verified purge (we return a request id and audit evidence when the run completes).

Attachments: I’ve attached a compact retention matrix that maps artifact types to default TTLs for hosted/dedicated/private.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Compliance & Trust
Redwood Inference

Vivek — thanks, this is great. A couple of quick asks so procurement can close the security checklist:
1) Please confirm whether "final response" includes any tool/function call arguments or tool outputs that the model returns as part of the text payload.
2) Can you add one sentence about whether we log token-level usage for billing vs. token-level content (i.e., do we store which tokens were consumed for billing, but not the token strings themselves?).

If we can get those clarifications I’ll publish a 1‑page summary to the public docs and share with Acme.

—Marissa
Sr. Product Manager, Privacy & Compliance

---- Message 4 (2028-05-12T14:30:00-07:00) ----
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.example.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>, Lina Park <lina.park@acme.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
Date: Sat, 12 May 2028 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on what Redwood stores by default (prompts/outputs)

Marissa — good points, adding precision below. Lina, looping you on the specifics we use internally.

On Fri, May 11, 2028 at 4:45 PM Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com> wrote:
> Vivek — thanks, this is great. A couple of quick asks so procurement can close the security checklist:
> 1) Please confirm whether "final response" includes any tool/function call arguments or tool outputs that the model returns as part of the text payload.
> 2) Can you add one sentence about whether we log token-level usage for billing vs. token-level content (i.e., do we store which tokens were consumed for billing, but not the token strings themselves?).

Reply (clarifications):
- Tool/function outputs: any text that is emitted to the client as part of the final response (including textified tool outputs or function-call arguments returned inline) is treated as part of the final response artifact and is retained under the same TTL (90 days by default for hosted). If a customer uses our structured "function-calls" feature and elects not to persist logs, those tool payloads are suppressed from the log store when the opt-out toggle is set.
- Token-level billing records: we emit aggregated token-usage counters (counts per request: prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens) to the billing system and those counters are kept for billing/finance records per our billing retention schedule. Those counters do not include the token strings themselves and cannot be reconstructed into the original content.

Action items (internal):
- Marissa: please take the two-line clarifications above and create a 1‑page procurement-ready summary (I recommend this exact language).
- Karthik: can you attach the short runbook for Data Erasure API to the retention matrix in the Drive link and flag any missing audit fields?

Vivek
